description: moneygram.com Revenue $1.24 Billion MoneyGram global money transfer network moving nearly $200 billion a year through almost 500,000 retail agent locations in 200+ countries and serving 60 million+ active customers, with over 70% of transactions now digital. It earns mainly from transfer fees plus currency exchange spreads, not from owning stores, since almost all locations are partner agents like post offices and grocery chains. In 2025 it cut 449 jobs to speed up digital growth and in 2026 launched its own MGUSD dollar stablecoin and a Visa card that spends digital dollars anywhere Visa works. MoneyGram owns no factories or stores, it is a licensed money transmitter with 75+ regulatory approvals, around 2,000 employees in 36 countries, and was taken private in 2023 for $1.8 billion.

placer.ai Revenue $136.5 Million private US company valued at $1.5 billion that sells foot traffic analytics for physical locations, estimating visits to stores, malls and offices from anonymized data on tens of millions of mobile phones with 92%+ claimed accuracy. It hit $100 million annual recurring revenue in 2024 after growing 80% in a year and serves 4,000+ customers including Sony, Wegmans, BJ's Wholesale, SeaWorld and Bloomberg, which puts Placer data into its Terminal so investors can track company performance before earnings. Money comes from SaaS subscriptions starting around $12,000 a year, API data feeds and add-on datasets, and it has raised $268 million in total funding. Around 630 employees work at Placer.ai after 150 layoffs in January 2025 aimed at reaching profitability, and it owns no factories or stores because its product is pure software and data.

kfc.com Revenue $36.4 Billion KFC runs 34,747 restaurants across 150+ countries and about 99% are franchised, run by local partners, serving roughly 1 billion chickens every year. Its restaurants sold $36.4 billion of food in 2025 with $1.5 billion in operating profit, earned mainly from 4-6% sales royalties paid by franchisees, not from selling chicken. 2025 was a record year with nearly 3,000 new restaurants opened across 105 countries, roughly one new KFC every 3 hours and 10,000 stores added in the last 5 years. KFC owns zero chicken farms or factories and buys from suppliers like Tyson Foods and Pilgrim's Pride with fresh deliveries up to 3 times a week. Around 30,000 corporate employees work for KFC worldwide while over 1 million people work across its franchise restaurants and supply network. A new U.S. KFC does about $1.5 million in average annual sales per restaurant and KFC is the world's #1 chicken chain by locations and sales.

rtaf.mi.th is the official portal of the Royal Thai Air Force, one of Asia's oldest air forces (founded November 2, 1913; independent since 1937), with ~46,000 personnel and 11 combat wings, now running a modern Odoo-based portal publishing financial reports, procurement plans, and White Papers on its "Unbeatable Air Force" roadmap to 2037. Its fleet spans 46 F-16s, 11 Gripen C/D, 13 F-5TH Super Tigris, Saab 340 Erieye AEW&C, C-130s, and a VIP fleet including an ex-Thai Airways A340-500. In July 2025 the RTAF fought its first combat since 1988 in the Thai-Cambodian border conflict, with its Gripens achieving the type's first-ever combat weapons launch. The centerpiece modernization is the Gripen E/F program: Thailand signed the $550M "Peace Burapha 1" contract in August 2025 — first in APAC — with deliveries from 2029 and 8 more jets sought toward a 12-aircraft squadron by 2037.
